newsitem.title: USA: The Hartford posts big first-quarter profit rise.
newsitem.headline: The Hartford posts big first-quarter profit rise.

text.p: The Hartford insurance company said Thursday its profits more than doubled in the first quarter, partly due to a mild winter that held North American losses down.

The net income of $204 million, equal to $1.73 a share, compared with $96 million, or 82 cents a share, in the first quarter of 1996, the company said. The results also topped Wall Street expectations of $1.49 a share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst estimates.
Revenues fell 6.6 percent to $3.1 billion from $3.3 billion a year ago.

The Hartford, Conn.-based company said catastrophe losses from North American property-casualty losses were $16 million after tax vs. $77 million a year ago. Most U.S. property-casualty insurers have benefited from a mild winter.
North American net income, excluding catastrophes, rose 17 percent to $120 million and revenues rose 3 percent to $1.605 billion compared with the year-ago quarter.
International net income fell 33 percent to $14 million despite an 8 percent rise in revenues to $417 million.
Life insurance net income rose 15 percent to $62 million although revenue fell 20 perecent to $996 million.
The Hartford, formerly ITT Hartford Group, was one of three companies formed in the 1995 divestiture of ITT Corp.
